title: performance-budgets
description: Learn about performance-budgets. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Performance budgets are systematic limits on the size and complexity of your web resources. They prevent performance regressions by ensuring that new features don't make your site slower. Budgets can be set for JavaScript bundles, CSS files, images, and total page weight.
Why Performance Budgets Matter

Without performance budgets, applications naturally become slower over time as features are added. Each new feature adds code, dependencies, and assets. Performance budgets provide guardrails that force teams to consider the performance impact of every change.

data.title: Performance Regression Example
data.code:
Without Performance Budgets:

Month 1: Initial launch
- JavaScript: 250KB
- CSS: 50KB
- Total: 300KB
- Load time: 2s

Month 3: Added analytics
- JavaScript: 450KB (+200KB)
- CSS: 50KB
- Total: 500KB
- Load time: 3.5s

Month 6: Added chat widget
- JavaScript: 850KB (+400KB)
- CSS: 120KB (+70KB)
- Total: 970KB
- Load time: 6s

Month 12: Multiple features
- JavaScript: 2.5MB
- CSS: 350KB
- Total: 2.85MB
- Load time: 15s

With Performance Budgets:
- JavaScript max: 400KB
- CSS max: 100KB
- Every addition requires optimization or removal

data.text: Types of Performance Budgets
1. Size Budgets
Size budgets limit the file size of specific resources. Common size budgets include maximum JavaScript bundle size, CSS file size, and individual asset sizes.

data.title: Size Budget Configuration
data.content: Set size limits for different resource types.

data.text: 2. Quantity Budgets
Quantity budgets limit the number of resources or requests. This prevents having too many small files that increase HTTP overhead.

data.title: Quantity Budget Examples
data.code:
Quantity Budget Examples:

- Maximum JavaScript files: 10
- Maximum CSS files: 3
- Maximum image requests: 20
- Maximum total requests: 50
- Maximum third-party scripts: 5

Rationale:
- Too many small files increase HTTP overhead
- Each request has DNS lookup, TCP connection, TLS overhead
- Browser limits parallel requests per domain
- Mobile networks have higher latency per request

data.text: 3. Time Budgets
Time budgets set maximum thresholds for load time metrics. These ensure the user experience remains acceptable even as features are added.

data.title: Time Budget Configuration
data.content: Set time limits for key performance metrics.

data.text: 4. Rule Budgets
Rule budgets enforce specific performance patterns or prohibit anti-patterns. Examples include banning layout shifts, requiring image optimization, or limiting synchronous scripts.

data.title: Rule Budget Examples
data.code:
Rule Budget Examples:

- No layout shifts (CLS must be 0)
- All images must be optimized (WebP/AVIF)
- No synchronous JavaScript in head
- All JavaScript must be minified
- No render-blocking resources
- All fonts must be preloaded
- No third-party scripts without consent
- All API calls must use compression

Enforcement:
- ESLint rules for code patterns
- Custom build scripts for resource checks
- Lighthouse CI for runtime violations
- Custom webpack plugins for bundle checks

data.text: Setting Realistic Budgets

Start by measuring your current performance, then set budgets slightly below your current metrics to drive improvement. Consider your target users' network conditions and devices when setting budgets.

data.title: Budget Calculation Process
data.content: Calculate budgets based on target performance.
data.code:
Budget Calculation Process:

1. Measure Current Performance
   - Current bundle size: 350KB
   - Current load time: 4.5s
   - Current CLS: 0.15

2. Define Target Performance
   - Target load time: 2.5s (45% improvement)
   - Target CLS: 0.05 (67% improvement)
   - Target bundle size: 200KB (43% reduction)

3. Calculate Budgets
   - JavaScript budget: 200KB
   - CSS budget: 50KB
   - Image budget: 100KB per image
   - CLS budget: 0.05
   - LCP budget: 2.5s

4. Consider User Context
   - Target network: 3G (1.6 Mbps)
   - Target device: Mid-range mobile
   - Target location: Global (varied latency)

5. Set Initial Budgets
   - Start with current metrics - 10%
   - Tighten gradually as you optimize
   - Use timeboxing to avoid over-optimization

data.text: Enforcing Performance Budgets
Integrate performance budget checks into your CI/CD pipeline to catch regressions before deployment. Use tools like Lighthouse CI, webpack performance hints, or custom scripts.

data.title: CI/CD Budget Enforcement
data.content: Add budget checks to your build process.

data.text: Budget Enforcement Strategies

items: Fail builds when budgets are exceeded (strict enforcement)
Warn when budgets are exceeded but allow manual override
Gradual budget tightening (start loose, tighten over time)
Exception process for necessary budget increases

data.title: Budget vs Business Needs
data.text: Performance budgets should support business goals, not block essential features. Have a process for approving budget increases when business value justifies it.
Monitoring Budget Compliance
Continuously monitor your performance budgets in production using real user monitoring (RUM). Set up alerts when budgets are exceeded to catch regressions quickly.

data.title: Production Budget Monitoring
data.content: Monitor budgets in production with RUM.

data.text: Budget Communication
Make performance budgets visible to the entire team. Display budget status in dashboards, include budget impact in code reviews, and celebrate when teams meet or exceed budget goals.

terms.definition: Systematic limits on resource sizes and complexity to prevent performance regressions as features are added.
Maximum file size limits for specific resource types like JavaScript bundles, CSS files, or images.
Maximum thresholds for load time metrics like LCP, CLS, or total blocking time.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Performance budgets prevent gradual performance degradation
Multiple budget types: size, quantity, time, and rule budgets
Set budgets based on current metrics and target performance
Enforce budgets in CI/CD to catch regressions before deployment
Monitor budgets in production with real user monitoring
Balance strict enforcement with business needs
Make budgets visible to the entire team
Tighten budgets gradually as optimization capabilities improve
data.takeaway: Performance budgets are essential guardrails that maintain user experience quality while enabling continued feature development.
